facts.raw_span: An 18-month-old girl was brought for evaluation of a swelling in her left medial thigh
the mass had enlarged gradually and was painless, with no history of trauma or infection
a firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
no signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests were unremarkable
a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh, extending toward the inguinal area
The lesion exhibited internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, displacing the common and superficial femoral vessels anterolaterally without signs of invasion
it abutted the proximal femoral bone but did not erode it
An MRI confirmed a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations and no encasement of neurovascular structures

concepts.why: The presence of a well-circumscribed, fatty-appearing mass with internal septations, as confirmed by MRI, is consistent with lipoblastoma, a rare benign tumor of adipose tissue that typically occurs in children.

The characteristics of the mass, including its fatty appearance, well-defined borders, and lack of invasion or erosion of surrounding structures, are also consistent with a lipoma, a common benign tumor of adipose tissue.
The presence of a well-defined, fatty-appearing mass with internal septations, as confirmed by imaging studies, could also suggest a hibernoma, a rare benign tumor of brown adipose tissue.

rationales.F02: Gradual enlargement and painlessness are more typical of benign tumors like lipoblastoma.
rationales.F03: A firm, nonpulsatile mass is consistent with a benign tumor like lipoblastoma or lipoma.
rationales.F06: A well-defined, lobulated mass is consistent with a benign fatty tumor.
rationales.F07: Internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat are characteristic of lipoblastoma and lipoma.
rationales.F08: The lack of bone erosion suggests a benign process.
rationales.F09: A fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations is highly suggestive of lipoblastoma or lipoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Lipoblastoma is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of a firm, nonpulsatile mass with internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat, which is consistent with the imaging findings, and the mass's gradual enlargement without signs of trauma or infection.
